ai.description: This slender sea snake reaches 105 cm. It is olive-grey above and yellow below, featuring 40–50 dark, narrow crossbands. A distinctive, narrow head and a yellow collar mark the nape.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Hydrophis stricticollis* is best distinguished by its unusually long, slender neck and a distinctively small head, which contrasts sharply with its thick, deep body.
ai.habitat: The Collared Sea Snake inhabits shallow coastal waters and estuaries along the Indian subcontinent, often frequenting murky, sediment-rich areas near river mouths.
ai.behavior: The Collared Sea Snake is primarily nocturnal, actively hunting for bottom-dwelling fish and eels in shallow coastal waters under the cover of darkness.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hydrophis stricticollis* is ovoviviparous, typically producing litters of 2–16 young. Breeding occurs throughout the year, peaking between February and May in India.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Collared Sea Snake inhabits coastal waters along the Indian subcontinent, ranging from the Bay of Bengal to the Arabian Sea, typically at sea level.
